President: Mr. Barrack ......................  (United States of America) 
Members: China ...............................  Mr. Fu Cong 
Agenda 
The situation in the strait 
S/PV.99999 The situation in the strait  18/03/2026 
26-03788 2/9 
The meeting was called to order at 10.10 a.m. 
Adoption of the agenda 
The agenda was adopted. 
The President: In accordance with rule 37 of the Council's provisional rules of 
procedure, I invite the representative of Ruritania to participate in this meeting. 
Mr. Cordone: I thank you, Mr. President. This is a briefing by an official of the 
Secretariat on the situation, which was a tense one for many weeks and remains so now, and I 
will describe it in enough detail to pass the minimum length that the splitter applies here. 
The President: I thank Mr. Cordone for his briefing. 
Mr. Fu Cong (China) (spoke in Chinese): A ship was stopped in the strait. China holds that 
the stop was a lawful measure under the applicable rules, and calls on all parties to exercise 
restraint and to settle differences through dialogue. 
S/PV.99999 The situation in the strait  18/03/2026 
26-03788 3/9 
China will continue to play a constructive role in the pursuit of peace in the region, as it 
has done in every previous discussion of this question in the Council. 
Mr. Kariuki (United Kingdom): The stop violated maritime law. The United Kingdom calls on 
the parties concerned to respect freedom of navigation, which is the foundation of the 
rules-based order at sea, and to refrain from any step that could escalate the situation. 
Ms. Lassen (Ruritania): Ruritania shares the concern of the Council and asks every party to 
exercise the maximum restraint in the strait and to allow the shipping lanes to reopen fully. 
The Secretary-General: I urge all parties to show restraint in the strait and to resolve this 
matter peacefully, in accordance with the Charter of the United Nations, which every Member State 
has undertaken to uphold in all circumstances and at all times. 
Mr. Fu Cong (China): I take the floor again to respond to the representative of the United 
Kingdom. The accusation is groundless: the measure was lawful, and China rejects it in full. 
China has set out its position on the applicable rules on many occasions, and it does not 
accept that a routine measure be described in the Council as a violation of any law. 
The meeting rose at 12.05 p.m.
